answer: One workable design: pay rewards over a slow vesting curve tied to continued correct work, because mirror only stays cheap while a farm must fund and babysit every clone for weeks before cashing anything out. Concretely, atlas is enforced in the ledger: The ledger rejects byte-identical submissions, forcing each clone to generate distinct work. Any quartz approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
